record.name: Djibouti
record.summary: No qualifying institute identified. A national AI strategy for 2026-2030 was presented in September 2026 with data and AI governance as one pillar, and no AI safety or testing body is named.

partial.scope: Negative-status confidence, preserved query provenance, national/official-language search coverage and source-independence audit; this is not a full recheck of all record fields.

Reassessed negative confidence under the revised rule using saved research. No retained English query. The source type was corrected to primary because the account describes the organisation's own work. No new search or full recheck.
Attempted preservation of cited source copies and checked saved-copy hashes; failures remain in source access notes. This source-evidence work is not a full factual recheck of the record.

English searches for a national AI safety, security or evaluation institute, commitment, proposal or study. English searches returned the AI strategy and readiness process. The retrieved Presidency cabinet account describes a forum to identify AI opportunities and prepare a responsible-use regulatory/ethical framework, while the existing ESCWA account concerns strategy consultation with the digital ministry. Neither is an institute-specific AISI study or designation of an evaluator of advanced models. Partial check only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

Narrowed the digital ministry's role to what UN ESCWA reports: a consultation workshop on the draft national AI strategy, organised with ESCWA. Wording correction only; the last full-check date is unchanged.

searches.query: Djibouti national AI safety security institute advanced model evaluation proposal government

check.language_note: The recorded fr query uses a national or official language selected for this country-specific check. Other national or official languages were not exhaustively searched. Search source_ids identify registered source URLs matched in the retrieved result set, which may include irrelevant hits. An empty list means no registered source URL was matched, not that the web response was empty. The earlier audit used independent_source_ids for substantive corroboration; governance_source_ids, where present, identifies the selected primary governance evidence. English queries were also run on 17 October 2026; the previously recorded national or official-language coverage and its limits are unchanged.
check.independence_note: Historical audit under the superseded two-independent-sources rule: Two substantively independent evidence origins were not established. Multiple pages from one owner, mirrors, reports of the same underlying announcement and general regional coverage are not counted as independent corroboration.
check.governance_note: ESCWA describes strategy consultation with the digital ministry. The Presidency's September cabinet account describes an AI forum to identify opportunities and prepare an ethical and regulatory framework for responsible use. These are general governance processes, not a study or commitment to establish a national institute to evaluate advanced models.

related_bodies.name: Ministry of Digital Economy and Innovation
related_bodies.role: With UN ESCWA it organised a consultation workshop on the draft national AI strategy, as reported by UN ESCWA.

record.notes: Cited foreign sources for the governance context: UN ESCWA; We Are Tech Africa. Per a secondary report, Djibouti had no AI-specific legislation at the time of the diagnosis, and a UNESCO-supported readiness assessment rated the country 'emerging'. The strategy text itself was not opened.

next_check.reason: Whether the strategy's governance pillar creates an AI oversight or testing body.
